open-question.question: The milestones tool's new `since` query finds a milestone's anchor, its latest `Starting-state:` commit, by subject and by the milestone's `requirements.md` path. Must the anchor carry the path-form subject `Starting-state: <path>` exactly, or does any commit whose subject opens with `Starting-state:` and that changed that file count, so that a starting state committed under the earlier bare-directory-name subject (as a live milestone kept in place by `/migrate-milestones` has) is still found?
open-question.alternative: The anchor is the latest commit whose subject is exactly `Starting-state: <path>`, the milestone's path with its trailing slash as resolution and the definition tool give it, among the commits that changed `<path>requirements.md`. A commit under any other descriptor, the earlier bare directory name included, is never read as an anchor, and the tool's help text states that limit as it states the id-form `Milestone-finish:` limit. Nothing is added for a live milestone the migration kept in place: it reads as having no starting state until a `Starting-state:` commit under its path lands. Matches how the tool already reads finish commits (only the path-form `Milestone-finish: <path>` subject counts, the id form never read), so the anchor rule is the one subject the workflow now writes, needs no legacy branch, and cannot take a hand-typed or stray `Starting-state:` subject as the anchor. The affected set is small and shrinks on its own: in this repository all 44 bare-name `Starting-state:` commits belong to finished milestones and both live milestones carry the path form, so only a migrated project's milestone that stayed live is affected, and only until it is finished or its starting state is recorded again under its path. A migrated project's live milestone whose starting state was recorded under the bare-name subject gets an empty `since` print, the "no starting state has been written" outcome, although its section is filled. The skill then runs a first run over a filled section, and the task-entry writers meet the no-anchor case, whose handling the sibling question on a missing anchor at task entry owns, so this option is only as harmless as that outcome makes it.

The anchor is the latest commit whose subject opens with `Starting-state:`, whatever follows the marker, among the commits that changed `<path>requirements.md`. The milestone is identified by the path-scoped file filter alone, as `tasks` selects every `Task-completion:` subject and identifies the milestone by the file list rather than by the subject's descriptor, so the bare-name subject an earlier release wrote is found the same way as the path form. A live milestone kept in place by `/migrate-milestones` keeps its recorded starting state as its anchor, so its first `since` call reads a refresh or a no-op rather than a first run, and the rule is one prefix test with no legacy form named in the tool: the commit tool scopes every `Starting-state:` commit to its own milestone's files, so the path filter already tells milestones apart, including two scopes holding one slug, whose bare names would collide. Any commit that changed the file under a `Starting-state:` subject counts, a hand-made one with a free descriptor included, so the anchor rule is looser than the path-form rule the finish read uses, and the tool reads two subject families by two different rules (`Milestone-finish:` by its exact path, `Starting-state:` by prefix), which the help text and the invariant have to state and justify.

The anchor is the latest commit, among those that changed `<path>requirements.md`, whose subject is exactly `Starting-state: <path>` or exactly `Starting-state: <name>`, `<name>` being the milestone directory's last path component, the bare-name form earlier releases wrote. A subject under any other descriptor is not read, and the help text names the two accepted forms. Finds every starting state either the current or an earlier release recorded, so a migrated live milestone keeps its anchor, while still refusing a stray or hand-typed `Starting-state:` subject whose descriptor names neither form; both forms are exact tests derived from the path the tool is given, with the file filter keeping a bare name that two scopes share from matching across them. Writes a legacy subject form into the tool permanently, a second accepted spelling with its own test fixtures and help-text sentence, kept for a population that only shrinks (migrated milestones that stayed live) and that the other history queries deliberately do not serve, since the finish read accepts the path form alone.

open-question.question: In a shallow clone the truncated log can omit a milestone's `Starting-state:` commit, so the new `since` query would read a recorded starting state as never written. Does `since` refuse a shallow repository as `gate` does, or read whatever the log yields with the limit stated only in its help text, as the history queries do?
open-question.alternative: `since` runs the same `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` test `gate` runs (the existing `is_shallow()` helper), before any log read and in both forms, the broad one and `--milestones`, and refuses on `true` with one `Error:` line naming `git fetch --unshallow` as the remedy, whatever the truncated log would have yielded. Its help text and the milestones-tool invariant then name two queries that check, `gate` and `since`, in place of "only `gate`". `since` is the starting-state procedure's opening call, so one refusal there stops the whole procedure before anything is read: a shallow clone can then neither report a recorded starting state as never written nor go on to the later `milestones` and `summary` reads, which the same truncated log would also make silently incomplete, and write a section grounded in a partial record. The case costs nothing at the task-entry writers, which check `gate` first and so already stop in a shallow clone before `since --milestones` runs; the check reuses a helper and a message the tool already has. It also refuses the shallow clones where the answer would have been right, any clone deep enough to hold the anchor, so `specify-milestone-starting-state` cannot run at all in a shallow checkout (a CI-style `--depth` clone, for instance) until it is unshallowed, and it widens a rule the third milestone settled as `gate` alone checking. What the skill does with the `Error:` line (a fixed stop line, or going on without the read) is the "Starting-state read failure" question's to settle.

`since` reads the log first and runs the shallow test only when it found no `Starting-state:` anchor for the milestone's `requirements.md`, refusing then with the same `Error:` line and `git fetch --unshallow` remedy; when the anchor was found it prints its lines as usual in a shallow clone and a complete one alike. The refusal applies to both forms, and the help text states that a shallow clone is refused only where the missing anchor might be truncation. It refuses exactly the one output the question names as wrong: a found anchor and every commit after it are newer than the anchor and so present in the truncated log, which makes those lines trustworthy, while "no line" is the only answer a shallow clone can falsify. A shallow clone deep enough to hold the anchor keeps working, and nothing is refused that would have been read correctly by `since` itself. The query's behaviour now depends on what it found as well as on the repository, a second code path and a refusal rule harder to state in one help-text sentence than either uniform form, and the protection ends at `since`: on a found anchor the procedure goes on to the `milestones` and `summary` reads, which the truncated log can still leave incomplete with no sign, so a refresh in a shallow clone may still miss older milestones. What the skill does on the refusal is the "Starting-state read failure" question's to settle.

`since` gets no shallow check: it prints whatever the truncated path-scoped log yields, with no stop line and no warning, exactly as `tasks`, `milestones`, `summary`, and `record` do, and its help text and the docs state the limit (a shallow clone can omit the anchor, which then reads as no starting state written). `gate` stays the one query that checks, and the invariant's "only `gate`" stands unchanged. It keeps the tool's settled split, `gate` alone checking because a gate passing silently lets two runs collide while a history reader wants what is there, and adds no code, no refusal, and no failure for any runner to handle. The missed anchor is mild in effect: the task-entry writers never reach `since` in a shallow clone because `gate` refuses first, and in `specify-milestone-starting-state` a missed anchor only turns a refresh or a no-op into a first run, which edits the section in place, leaving byte-identical every subsection whose facts still hold, and lands a new `Starting-state:` commit that becomes the anchor from then on. In a shallow clone the skill misreads a recorded starting state as never written with no sign to anyone, pays an exploration the no-op line would have spared, and may write prose for unchanged facts that the next review pass reads as change; the later record reads it explores with are truncated just as silently, so the refreshed section can be grounded in a partial history and nothing tells the operator to unshallow.

open-question.question: `since` is to list every commit after the anchor that touched the milestone's scope outside the milestone's own directory. Another live milestone's directory in the same container, or in one nested below, lies inside that scope, so its definition, review, annotation, and answer commits would each read as the ground having moved. In the broad form (without `--milestones`), do commits that change only files inside another milestone's directory count, or are they left out?

The planned `show MILESTONE_PATH FILE` query prints one of a milestone's three files as it stood at the finish commit's parent, or as it stands now when the milestone is live. Finish requires an empty question document and a task list holding no section, so at a finish commit's parent only `requirements.md` holds content, and a milestone from before the question-document split has no `open_questions.xml` there at all. Which files does `show` serve: all three by a FILE argument (and then what does it do for a file that parent does not hold), or `requirements.md` alone?

The starting-state procedure reads `live` filtered to its milestone's scope and the `milestones` overview on that scope, and the review pass reads the same overview, but each runner holds only the milestone's path (`<scope>/milestones/<slug>/`). Is the scope passed as a directory the runner derives from that path itself (`.` for the root), or do the two queries accept the milestone's path and derive its scope in the tool, as `gate` does; and does the filtered `live` print include the milestone the runner is working in?

The starting state's record read has two tiers: the `milestones` overview on the scope, then a deeper read through `summary` or `show` of the milestones whose title bears on the goal. Neither prints a completed task's verified bar, which only `tasks <path> --with-body` does, and only for tasks completed since bars moved into commit bodies. Does the deeper read include that bar read for the milestones that bear, or stop at their summaries and recorded decisions?

The starting state is explored with the milestone's goal as its filter, but `since` looks only at commits outside the milestone's own directory, so a `Goal-revision:` commit made after the latest `Starting-state:` commit leaves the anchor line standing alone and `specify-milestone-starting-state` would end on its no-op line without exploring. Does a goal revision recorded after the anchor count as a reason to explore again?

A refresh that explores and finds nothing to change in the `## Relevant starting state` section lands no commit, so the anchor stays where it was and every later run in the same stale window (the skill run again, or the next `derive-tasks` or `submit-task` entry) explores again. How is that repeated exploration bounded, if at all?

The starting-state procedure opens with the milestones tool's `since` query and then reads the record and what is in flight through `milestones`, `summary`, `show`, and `live`. When one of those calls fails (the tool refuses, or git is unavailable), what does each of the procedure's three runners (`specify-milestone-starting-state`, `derive-tasks`, `submit-task`) do: stop on a fixed line with nothing written, or go on without that read?

During a refresh the starting-state procedure clears the standing picks the changed facts undermine with one `strip --recommendation` call, made after the section has been edited. When that call fails, does the runner stop with the edit left uncommitted, as `modify-milestone-goal` does on its own failed clearing call, or commit the refreshed section with the picks left standing; and does the same hold inside `derive-tasks` and `submit-task`, where a stale state is meant never to stop the writer?

`derive-tasks` and `submit-task` are to refresh the starting state when `since --milestones` prints a line beyond the anchor line. When it prints nothing at all, because the milestone has no `Starting-state:` commit (the step was skipped, or the section was written by hand or arrived in the milestone's first commit), does the writer follow the starting-state procedure as a first run and commit it, or go on to its own write with the section as it stands?

`derive-tasks` and `submit-task` check the scope gate directly ahead of their write call today, after their reads and their authoring. The staleness check has to follow the gate and precede those reads, which moves the gate to the front of each writer. Is the gate then checked once, at the front, or again directly before the write call as well, now that the reads, a possible refresh, and the authoring stand between the check and the write?

The review pass is to read the `milestones` overview on its milestone's scope, bounded to the recent milestones, on every pass, but the `milestones` query takes no bound today and prints every milestone that ever touched the scope (56 lines on this repository's root). How is that overview bounded to the recent ones?

The review pass gains one fixed call to the milestones tool at its inventory step, the `milestones` overview. When that call fails (the tool refuses, or git is unavailable), does the pass stop on a fixed line of its own before changing anything, or report the failure and carry on reviewing from the milestone's two documents alone?

Each of the three chains on the ways-of-using page that derive and complete tasks ("Answering the questions that matter to you", "Putting more intelligence into a stuck milestone", "Executing tasks") is to open with the refresh line and one review pass. A question that review raises needs an alternatives line, a recommend line, and an answer line before `derive-tasks` will run, and two of the three chains carry no alternatives line today. What lines does each of those chains carry between its opening review and its derivation line?

The benchmark draft's two cairn deliveries each run one unbroken chain per phase: the starting-state line, the bounded review loop, then the derivation line directly behind the loop. Once every execution chain on the ways-of-using page opens with the refresh line and a review pass, do the benchmark deliveries gain a second starting-state line ahead of their derivation line, or keep the one they have?

The host-suite test needs `derive-tasks` to find its milestone's scope free and its starting state stale, which takes a second, overlapping milestone whose task or finish commits land after the first milestone's `Starting-state:` commit and which no longer holds the scope when `derive-tasks` runs. Is that second milestone seeded as already finished in the seeded repository's history, or left live in the seed and finished through the host by the test before it derives?

The new host-suite test is to assert the refresh on all three hosts, but the suite runs on demand, outside CI, and can pass on a host only after the rebuilt tree is committed and that host's installed plugin copy is refreshed by hand. Does completing this milestone require a passing run of the test against each of the three hosts, the task that runs it refreshing the installed copies first, or only that the test is delivered and passes on the hosts available when it lands?
